ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle C=90^\circ$, $\angle ABC=70^\circ$. Point D is the midpoint of AB, and point E is a moving point on side AC. $\triangle ADE$ is folded along DE, placing point A at point A'. When $A'E \parallel BC$, then what is the degree measure of $\angle ADE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, when $A'E\parallel BC$,\\
$\therefore \angle A'EA=\angle C=90^\circ$,\\
$\because \angle ABC=70^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle A=90^\circ-70^\circ=20^\circ$,\\
By folding, we know: $\angle A'ED=\angle AED=\frac{1}{2}\angle A'EA=45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle ADE=180^\circ-\angle A-\angle AED=180^\circ-20^\circ-45^\circ=\boxed{115^\circ}$.

method.method_draft: Use direct angle chasing with the fold crease as an angle bisector. First read from the diagram that AC is horizontal, BC is vertical, E lies on AC, D lies on AB, and the folded point A' is positioned so that A'E is drawn parallel to BC. From the text, use ∠C = 90° and ∠ABC = 70° to get ∠A = 20°. Since A'E ∥ BC and AE lies on AC, A'E is perpendicular to AE, so ∠A'EA = 90°. Folding along DE reflects A to A', so DE is the mirror line and bisects the angle between EA and EA'; hence ∠AED = ∠A'ED = 45°. In triangle ADE, compute ∠ADE = 180° − ∠DAE − ∠AED = 180° − 20° − 45° = 115°.

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle C=90^\circ$, $\angle ABC=70^\circ$. Point D is the midpoint of AB, and point E is a moving point on side AC. $\triangle ADE$ is folded along DE, placing point A at point A'. When $A'E \parallel BC$, then what is the degree measure of $\angle ADE$?
ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, when $A'E\parallel BC$,\\
$\therefore \angle A'EA=\angle C=90^\circ$,\\
$\because \angle ABC=70^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle A=90^\circ-70^\circ=20^\circ$,\\
By folding, we know: $\angle A'ED=\angle AED=\frac{1}{2}\angle A'EA=45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle ADE=180^\circ-\angle A-\angle AED=180^\circ-20^\circ-45^\circ=\boxed{115^\circ}$

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure, on the left there is vertical BC, the base AC is horizontal to the right, and C is the right-angle vertex; A is on the right side, B is on the upper left, and AB slants downward to the right. D is marked on AB, and E is marked on AC. The folded point A′ is on the upper left, and A′D, A′E, and DE are connected in the figure, and the given condition of the problem gives discussing the angle when A′E ∥ BC.
Reasoning: Because ∠C=90°, ∠ABC=70°, therefore ∠A=180°−90°−70°=20°. Also because A′E ∥ BC, and AE is on AC, while BC ⟂ AC, therefore A′E ⟂ AE, that is, ∠A′EA=90°. The folding is carried out along DE, and A is reflected to A′, therefore DE is the angle bisector of the angle between EA and EA′, so ∠AED=∠A′ED=45°. In △ADE, ∠DAE=∠A=20°, ∠AED=45°, therefore ∠ADE=180°−20°−45°=115°.
